questions.stem: Detachment of myosin head from actin is caused by:

options.label: B
options.text: Attachment of ATP to the head

options.label: C
options.text: Binding of ADP and IP to head

questions.answerText: Attachment of ATP to the head
questions.solutionHtml:
Attachment of ATP to the head

When ATP binds to the myosin head, it leads to the detachment of the myosin head from actin.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Pg no: 104.

questions.stem: Increased release of Ach can occur by:-

options.label: A
options.text: Blocking Na+ channels on presynaptic membrane

options.label: B
options.text: Blocking K+ channels on presynaptic membrane

options.label: C
options.text: Blocking leaky Cl- channels on presynaptic

options.label: D
options.text: Blocking Ca2+ channels on presynaptic membrane

questions.answerText: Blocking K+ channels on presynaptic membrane
questions.solutionHtml:
Blocking K+ channels on presynaptic membrane
  • When K+ (potassium) channels on the presynaptic membrane are blocked, it leads to membrane depolarization. Normally, after an action potential reaches the presynaptic terminal, it triggers the opening of voltage-gated Ca2+ (calcium) channels.
  • The entry of Ca2+ into the presynaptic terminal is essential for the release of neurotransmitters, including ACh, into the synaptic cleft.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no. 97, 68.

questions.stem: What happens in case of "Vasopressin escape" on SIADH?
questions.solutionHtml:
Down regulation of Aquaporin 2 receptors

When SIADH persists over time, the kidneys become less responsive to the effects of ADH, leading to downregulation of the aquaporin 2 (AQP2) receptors in the collecting ducts of the kidney tubules.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 688.

questions.stem: If lung was allowed to recoil without the chest wall in expiration what would be the resultant lung volume?
questions.solutionHtml:
Minimal value

In this scenario, the lung would reach its minimal volume, which is the point at which its elastic forces are balanced, but no further air can be expelled without active effort.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 622, Costanzo's physiology 6th edition Page no: 201

questions.stem: You are an intern and want to determine the quantity of IV fluids needed for a patient. How much amount of transient loss/insensible loss per day would your account for in your calculations?
questions.solutionHtml:
500-600 ml/day

The range of 500-600 ml/day (Option D) represents an estimation of typical insensible losses in a healthy adult at normal environmental conditions.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page no: 913.
